title: Online Learning to Rank under Corruption: A Robust Cascading Bandits Approach

problem.claim: Online learning-to-rank systems must recommend short ranked lists while learning from user clicks to maximize the likelihood of at least one click over many timesteps.

gap.claim: Cascading-bandit systems are vulnerable to click fraud and other corruptions that mislead learning and degrade user experience.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes M2UCB-V, a robust algorithm using a mean-of-medians estimator for bandits with corruption.
The estimator behaves like a standard mean without corruption and filters outliers and corrupted samples under corruption.
M2UCB-V achieves optimal logarithmic regret without corruption and degrades gracefully under corruption with an additive term tied to total corruption.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that, to their knowledge, the mean-of-medians estimator is applied to bandits with corruption for the first time.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Updating the estimator every round accelerates empirical convergence in experiments.
Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show consistent outperformance of prior methods while maintaining strong robustness.
The approach reportedly improves regret by 97.35% and 91.60% over two state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Online learning to rank recommends short ranked lists and learns from user clicks.
Cascading bandits model the objective as maximizing the likelihood of at least one click across timesteps.
Click fraud and related corruptions inject misleading feedback and degrade user experience.
M2UCB-V uses a mean-of-medians estimator that acts like a standard mean without corruption and filters corrupted samples under corruption.
The authors report favorable regret behavior, empirical convergence, and improvements over prior methods on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Corrupted click feedback can mislead online ranking systems and degrade user experience.

interpretation.claim: Learning systems that depend on user feedback should account for adversarial or manipulated observations.

application.claim: Robust estimators such as mean-of-medians can be considered for ranking systems exposed to click manipulation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the corruption assumptions or the conditions under which the robustness guarantee applies.

unknowns: The corruption model and assumptions are unspecified.
The regret definition, horizon, and formal guarantee details are unspecified.
The real-world datasets and experimental protocol are unspecified.
The two state-of-the-art baselines are unspecified.
Implementation details for the mean-of-medians estimator are unspecified.
